figures.caption: Figure 2: Training dynamics of the three reward-design iterations. (a) Reward: v3 climbs faster and levels off higher; v1 and v2 plateau together. (b) KL-to-reference: v1’s reward-layer scaling drives KL to ∼0.31; v2/v3 hold at 0.09/0.15. (c) Tool-use turns: v3 stabilizes at ∼2.1; v1 and v2 rebound to ∼2.6 after step 500.
Table 4: Comparison of CATM (ours) with LRAT (Zhou et al., 2026).

Figure 3: Three-layer RL environment. Layer 1 extracts unique (repo, commit) pairs; Layer 2 uses git clone –bare and git worktree add to share the .git object database across commits; Layer 3 executes grep/glob/read through native subprocesses with safety guards. The right-hand sidebar compares against a Docker sandbox.

Table 3: Downstream comparison of the baseline, BM25 top-2, Jina-1.5B top-2, and CodeGrep v1/v2/v3 on SWEBench Verified. Efficiency columns (Resolved r., Resolved tok., Unresolved r.) are averaged over each configuration’s own resolved / unresolved set.

Figure 4: Training-stability diagnostics over the same ∼900 GRPO steps as Figure 2, for all three reward iterations. (a) Mean completion length: v2 inflates dramatically (smoothed peak ∼ 1,150 tokens near step 450; raw peak ∼2000), v1 shows a milder mid-training bump, and v3 stays near 300–400 throughout. (b) Gradient norms remain bounded throughout for all three. (c) Completion-clipping ratio mirrors the length curve: v2 peaks at ∼20%, v1 at ∼14%, and v3 stays below 6% throughout.

Figure 1: System overview. Training (blue) produces CodeGrep weights from open-source agent trajectories via GRPO. Inference (orange) uses the trained CodeGrep as a retrieval submodule whose output is injected into a frozen downstream agent’s prompt.
